evals.prompt: I keep re-explaining to you how we run database migrations in this repo (always dry-run first with `bin/migrate --plan`, then apply, then run the smoke tests in tests/smoke). Turn that into a skill I can install with npx skills.
evals.expected_output: A folder <name>/SKILL.md with a trigger-first description, a short body with the three steps and completion criteria, the exact commands as low-freedom steps, and evals/evals.json with at least three prompts. No README inside the skill.
expectations: Creates <name>/SKILL.md where frontmatter name equals the folder name
Description is third person and contains a 'Use when' style trigger clause naming migrations, schema changes, or the migrate command
Description does not enumerate the three workflow steps
Body is under 150 lines and gives the dry-run, apply, and smoke-test commands verbatim
evals/evals.json exists with at least three evals
scripts/validate_skill.py was run on the result and reports zero errors

evals.prompt: My wp-components skill (skills/wp-components/SKILL.md in this repo) never fires. When I ask about inspector controls or a Gutenberg modal it just answers from memory. Fix the triggering.
evals.expected_output: A rewritten description that front-loads the leading concept, adds the user's real phrasing (inspector controls, modal, Gutenberg, @wordpress/components), adds a pushy 'even if' clause and a near-miss hand-off, plus a set of should/should-not trigger prompts to test with.
expectations: Only the description changes materially; the body is not rewritten
New description mentions at least three concrete trigger phrases the user used
New description includes a near-miss boundary or hand-off to a sibling skill
A trigger eval set with should_trigger true and false entries is produced, and the false entries share vocabulary with the skill
The agent proposes testing on a fresh agent rather than declaring the fix done

evals.prompt: Before I install github.com/someone/deploy-helper-skill into the client repo, clone it and check it over. It has a scripts/ folder and asks for allowed-tools Bash(*).
evals.expected_output: An audit report ordered by severity with path:line, what each finding does, and what to change; a clear install / do-not-install recommendation.
expectations: Runs scripts/validate_skill.py on the skill before the manual pass
Flags allowed-tools Bash(*) as a High finding with a scoped alternative
Reads every file under scripts/ and reports network calls, env reads, and writes outside the working directory
Searches SKILL.md and references for instructions aimed at the model unrelated to deploying
Ends with an explicit recommendation and does not install anything with a Critical or High finding
